NKJV.1: “Is there not a time of hard service for man on earth? Are not his days also like the days of a hired man?
NKJV.2: Like a servant who earnestly desires the shade, And like a hired man who eagerly looks for his wages,
NKJV.3: So I have been allotted months of futility, And wearisome nights have been appointed to me.
NKJV.4: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, And the night be ended?’ For I have had my fill of tossing till dawn.
NKJV.5: My flesh is caked with worms and dust, My skin is cracked and breaks out afresh.
NKJV.6: “My  days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, And are spent without hope.
NKJV.7: Oh, remember that my life is a breath! My eye will never again see good.
NKJV.8: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more; While your eyes are upon me, I shall no longer be.
NKJV.9: As the cloud disappears and vanishes away, So he who goes down to the grave does not come up.
NKJV.10: He shall never return to his house,  Nor shall his place know him anymore.
NKJV.11: “Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
NKJV.12: Am I a sea, or a sea serpent, That You set a guard over me?
NKJV.13: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me, My couch will ease my complaint,’
NKJV.14: Then You scare me with dreams And terrify me with visions,
NKJV.15: So that my soul chooses strangling And death rather than my body.
NKJV.16: I loathe my life; I would not live forever. Let me alone, For my days are but a breath.
NKJV.17: “What is man, that You should exalt him, That You should set Your heart on him,
NKJV.18: That You should visit him every morning, And test him every moment?
NKJV.19: How long? Will You not look away from me, And let me alone till I swallow my saliva?
NKJV.20: Have I sinned? What have I done to You, O watcher of men? Why have You set me as Your target, So that I am a burden to myself?
NKJV.21: Why then do You not pardon my transgression, And take away my iniquity? For now I will lie down in the dust, And You will seek me diligently, But I will no longer be.”

ESV.1: “Has not man a hard service on earth, and are not his days like the days of a hired hand?
ESV.2: Like a slave who longs for the shadow, and like a hired hand who looks for his wages,
ESV.3: so I am allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery are apportioned to me.
ESV.4: When I lie down I say, ‘When shall I arise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing till the dawn.
ESV.5: My flesh is clothed with worms and dirt; my skin hardens, then breaks out afresh.
ESV.6: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle and come to their end without hope.
ESV.7: “Remember that my life is a breath; my eye will never again see good.
ESV.8: The eye of him who sees me will behold me no more; while your eyes are on me, I shall be gone.
ESV.9: As the cloud fades and vanishes, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come up;
ESV.10: he returns no more to his house, nor does his place know him anymore.
ESV.11: “Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
ESV.12: Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?
ESV.13: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me, my couch will ease my complaint,’
ESV.14: then you scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
ESV.15: so that I would choose strangling and death rather than my bones.
ESV.16: I loathe my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
ESV.17: What is man, that you make so much of him, and that you set your heart on him,
ESV.18: visit him every morning and test him every moment?
ESV.19: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone till I swallow my spit?
ESV.20: If I sin, what do I do to you, you watcher of mankind? Why have you made me your mark? Why have I become a burden to you?
ESV.21: Why do you not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For now I shall lie in the earth; you will seek me, but I shall not be.”

NLT.1:
“Is not all human life a struggle?
Our lives are like that of a hired hand,
NLT.2:
like a worker who longs for the shade,
like a servant waiting to be paid.
NLT.3:
I, too, have been assigned months of futility,
long and weary nights of misery.
NLT.4:
Lying in bed, I think, ‘When will it be morning?’
But the night drags on, and I toss till dawn.
NLT.5:
My body is covered with maggots and scabs.
My skin breaks open, oozing with pus.
NLT.6:
“My days fly faster than a weaver’s shuttle.
They end without hope.
NLT.7:
O God, remember that my life is but a breath,
and I will never again feel happiness.
NLT.8:
You see me now, but not for long.
You will look for me, but I will be gone.
NLT.9:
Just as a cloud dissipates and vanishes,
those who die will not come back.
NLT.10:
They are gone forever from their home —
never to be seen again.
NLT.11:
“I cannot keep from speaking.
I must express my anguish.
My bitter soul must complain.
NLT.12:
Am I a sea monster or a dragon
that you must place me under guard?
NLT.13:
I think, ‘My bed will comfort me,
and sleep will ease my misery,’
NLT.14:
but then you shatter me with dreams
and terrify me with visions.
NLT.15:
I would rather be strangled —
rather die than suffer like this.
NLT.16:
I hate my life and don’t want to go on living.
Oh, leave me alone for my few remaining days.
NLT.17:
“What are people, that you should make so much of us,
that you should think of us so often?
NLT.18:
For you examine us every morning
and test us every moment.
NLT.19:
Why won’t you leave me alone,
at least long enough for me to swallow!
NLT.20:
If I have sinned, what have I done to you,
O watcher of all humanity?
Why make me your target?
Am I a burden to you?
NLT.21:
Why not just forgive my sin
and take away my guilt?
For soon I will lie down in the dust and die.
When you look for me, I will be gone.”

MSG.1:
"Human life is a struggle, isn't it?
It's a life sentence to hard labor.
MSG.2:
Like field hands longing for quitting time
and working stiffs with nothing to hope for but payday,
MSG.3:
I'm given a life that meanders and goes nowhere—
months of aimlessness, nights of misery!
MSG.4:
I go to bed and think, 'How long till I can get up?'
I toss and turn as the night drags on—and I'm fed up!
MSG.5:
I'm covered with maggots and scabs.
My skin gets scaly and hard, then oozes with pus.
MSG.6:
My days come and go swifter than the click of knitting needles,
and then the yarn runs out—an unfinished life!
MSG.7:
"God, don't forget that I'm only a puff of air!
These eyes have had their last look at goodness.
MSG.8:
And your eyes have seen the last of me;
even while you're looking, there'll be nothing left to look at.
MSG.9:
When a cloud evaporates, it's gone for good;
those who go to the grave never come back.
MSG.10:
They don't return to visit their families;
never again will friends drop in for coffee.
MSG.11:
"And so I'm not keeping one bit of this quiet,
I'm laying it all out on the table;
my complaining to high heaven is bitter, but honest.
MSG.12:
Are you going to put a muzzle on me,
the way you quiet the sea and still the storm?
MSG.13:
If I say, 'I'm going to bed, then I'll feel better.
A little nap will lift my spirits,'
MSG.14:
You come and so scare me with nightmares
and frighten me with ghosts
MSG.15:
That I'd rather strangle in the bedclothes
than face this kind of life any longer.
MSG.16:
I hate this life! Who needs any more of this?
Let me alone! There's nothing to my life—it's nothing
but smoke.
MSG.17:
"What are mortals anyway, that you bother with them,
that you even give them the time of day?
MSG.18:
That you check up on them every morning,
looking in on them to see how they're doing?
MSG.19:
Let up on me, will you?
Can't you even let me spit in peace?
MSG.20:
Even suppose I'd sinned—how would that hurt you?
You're responsible for every human being.
Don't you have better things to do than pick on me?
Why make a federal case out of me?
MSG.21:
Why don't you just forgive my sins
and start me off with a clean slate?
The way things are going, I'll soon be dead.
You'll look high and low, but I won't be around."

NRSVCE.9:
As the cloud fades and vanishes,
so those who go down to Sheol do not come up;
NRSVCE.10:
they return no more to their houses,
nor do their places know them any more.
NRSVCE.11:
“Therefore I will not restrain my mouth;
I will speak in the anguish of my spirit;
I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
NRSVCE.12:
Am I the Sea, or the Dragon,
that you set a guard over me?
NRSVCE.13:
When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me,
my couch will ease my complaint,’
NRSVCE.14:
then you scare me with dreams
and terrify me with visions,
NRSVCE.15:
so that I would choose strangling
and death rather than this body.
NRSVCE.16:
I loathe my life; I would not live forever.
Let me alone, for my days are a breath.
NRSVCE.17:
What are human beings, that you make so much of them,
that you set your mind on them,
NRSVCE.18:
visit them every morning,
test them every moment?
NRSVCE.19:
Will you not look away from me for a while,
let me alone until I swallow my spittle?
NRSVCE.20:
If I sin, what do I do to you, you watcher of humanity?
Why have you made me your target?
Why have I become a burden to you?
NRSVCE.21:
Why do you not pardon my transgression
and take away my iniquity?
For now I shall lie in the earth;
you will seek me, but I shall not be.”

NET.1: “Does not humanity have hard service on earth? Are not their days also like the days of a hired man?
NET.2: Like a servant longing for the evening shadow, and like a hired man looking for his wages,
NET.3: thus I have been made to inherit months of futility, and nights of sorrow have been appointed to me.
NET.4: If I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise?’, and the night stretches on and I toss and turn restlessly until the day dawns.
NET.5: My body is clothed with worms and dirty scabs; my skin is broken and festering.
NET.6: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle and they come to an end without hope.
NET.7: Remember that my life is but a breath, that my eyes will never again see happiness.
NET.8: The eye of him who sees me now will see me no more; your eyes will look for me, but I will be gone.
NET.9: As a cloud is dispersed and then disappears, so the one who goes down to the grave does not come up again.
NET.10: He returns no more to his house, nor does his place of residence know him any more.
NET.11: “Therefore, I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
NET.12: Am I the sea, or the creature of the deep, that you must put me under guard?
NET.13: If I say, “My bed will comfort me, my couch will ease my complaint,”
NET.14: then you scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
NET.15: so that I would prefer strangling, and death more than life.
NET.16: I loathe it; I do not want to live forever; leave me alone, for my days are a vapor!
NET.17: “What is mankind that you make so much of them, and that you pay attention to them?
NET.18: And that you visit them every morning, and try them every moment?
NET.19: Will you never look away from me, will you not let me alone long enough to swallow my spittle?
NET.20: If I have sinned — what have I done to you, O watcher of men? Why have you set me as your target? Have I become a burden to you?
NET.21: And why do you not pardon my transgression, and take away my iniquity? For now I will lie down in the dust, and you will seek me diligently, but I will be gone.”
